NWPD Search for Missing Person Christopher
content:
New Westminster –
The New Westminster Police Department is seeking public assistance in locating a missing person, Christopher.
Christopher is described as a 31 year-old Indigenous male, 5’10” tall, medium build, short brown hair and brown eyes. Christopher also wears eye glasses.
“We simply want to confirm Christopher’s well-being,” stated Sergeant Andrew Leaver. “His loved ones are worried that they haven’t heard from him.”
Christopher may be taking public transit and has also been known to spend time in Vancouver. If you have any information about Christopher’s location, please call the New Westminster Police Department at 604-525-5411. If you see Christopher we ask that you call 9-1-1.

title: Sexual Exploitation Investigation Leads Police to Multiple Weapons Seizure
Man with replica handgun sparks heavy police response near New Westminster SkyTrain Station
content:
New Westminster – On May 26th, 2026 at approximately 8:15pm a passerby noticed a male who they believed to be in possession of a handgun in the parking garage at 800 Carnarvon Street, New Westminster. The New Westminster Police Department responded and contained the area.
The male was safely taken into custody and found to be in possession of a holstered replica firearm and magazines. The male was transported to hospital to be treated for existing injuries and was released on an undertaking with numerous firearm-related conditions.
The incident caused a temporary disruption to the area, including the transit system. Police would like to thank the public for their patience while this matter was being resolved. “These types of incidents are extremely dynamic, and measures were put into place to make sure that the public were kept safe as the event unfolded” stated Sergeant Andrew Leaver. This incident required numerous police resources, and the New Westminster Police Department would like to thank the RCMP Integrated Police Dog Services, the Metro Vancouver Transit Police, and the Burnaby RCMP for their assistance.
When police respond to any call involving a firearm, it is treated as legitimate until an investigation can determine otherwise. “These replicas look extremely realistic, and being in possession of them can have serious consequences” stated Sergeant Leaver. For the safety of our communities, the New Westminster Police Department strongly discourages the purchase and use of these items.

title: Multiple vehicles taken out of service during Commercial Vehicle Enforcement event
content:
New Westminster –
On May 13th, 2026, the New Westminster Police Department Traffic Unit, along with other community safety partners, conducted a Commercial Vehicle safety inspection event along the 500 block of Royal Avenue in New Westminster.
Working alongside the Port Moody Police Department, Delta Police Department, Metro Vancouver Transit Police, the RCMP Integrated Road Safety Unit, and Langley Township Bylaw Commercial Vehicle Enforcement, officers use their specialized expertise to inspect 23 commercial vehicles.
Of the vehicles that were inspected, 8 were taken out of service due to various mechanical or safety concerns, 4 vehicles were found to have insecure loads, and 1 vehicle was determined to be overweight. In total, 24 Provincial Violation tickets were issued for infractions noted during the inspections.
“We all have a part to play in keeping our roads safe,” stated Sergeant Andrew Leaver. “We’re grateful to work alongside our community safety partners, who bring valuable expertise to these checks. Their knowledge and training help ensure we’re identifying serious risks before they lead to a collision.”
Police would like to remind commercial vehicle operators to ensure that their vehicles are in compliant operating conditions before starting their trips.
The New Westminster Police Department thanks all partner agencies involved for helping make this enforcement initiative a success.

title: Officers arrest armed man after woman stabbed
content:
New Westminster –
On May 6 at approximately 11:00pm the New Westminster Police Department received a 9-1-1 call from someone describing a woman being slashed with a knife. The caller shared that two men were fleeing the scene and they provided descriptions of the suspects. Officers rushed to the New Westminster SkyTrain station to provide aid to the woman who was found with a laceration.
Within minutes, officers located two men matching the suspect descriptions on Columbia Street. When officers called out to the men, they split up and ran in different directions. After two foot pursuits the suspects quickly found themselves in police custody. One of the suspects was found to be in possession of a loaded handgun, drugs, and several thousands of dollars of counterfeit currency.
“We’d like to thank the caller who made the decision to call 9-1-1,” stated Media Relations Officer Sergeant Andrew Leaver. “Anyone can make the choice to be an active bystander and help victims of crime by relaying important information about what you’re seeing to police.”
The victim was transported to hospital by BC Emergency Health Services Paramedics. At this stage in the investigation, it is unclear what relationship, if any, exists between the victim and the suspects.

title: Multiple reports made after man seen with handgun-style lighter
content:
New Westminster –
On April 21st
at approximately 1:00 pm a member of the public attended the front counter of the New Westminster Police Department to share they saw someone who they believed to be in possession of a handgun on Clarkson Street. Moments later, a call was made to 9-1-1 describing a similar suspect with a black handgun.
Officers quickly located a man on Clarkson Street matching the suspect description. An NWPD drone was deployed to get a closer look at the suspect. The footage from the NWPD drone helped officers in determining the handgun was a butane lighter shaped like a handgun. The use of the NWPD drone avoided what would have been a much larger and higher-risk police response.
“These handgun-shaped lighters continue to be a source of calls to 9-1-1,” stated Sergeant Andrew Leaver. “When someone brandishes something that looks like a handgun in a public setting they’re putting themselves and everyone around them at risk.”
Officers had a conversation with the man about the distress his butane lighter caused people in the area. The man handed the lighter to police for disposal. Easily mistaken for real firearms, handgun-shaped lighters can escalate police interactions and prompt 9-1-1 calls that are prioritized, resulting in elevated police response.

title: NWPD search for missing person Gordon “Dale” Raymond who was last seen in 1987
content:
New Westminster –
The New Westminster Police Department is seeking public assistance in determining the whereabouts of Gordon Raymond who was last seen in 1987. His family and friends have not seen or heard from him since. Mr. Raymond was commonly known as “Dale,” and sometimes “Gord.”
Mr. Raymond was 39 years old at the time of his disappearance and would be 79 years old today. In the 1980s he lived throughout the Metro Vancouver region, including Surrey, Vancouver, and New Westminster. He has previously lived in Edmonton, Alberta and Thailand. He is described as a Caucasian male, standing 6’2” tall, with top and bottom false teeth, and surgery scars from a broken hip and an appendectomy. He was known to work as an aircraft mechanic and drove a cream 1976 Buick Century, similar to the one pictured below. In 1986 he painted the rear windows of his car black, and may have slept in his vehicle. Mr. Raymond had a son, Gordon Jr., who police are hoping to speak to.
“We are committed to supporting this investigation and finding Mr. Raymond,” stated Sergeant Andrew Leaver. “His family is hoping for answers. Please, be a force multiplier and let’s work together to share this appeal for information.”
Mr. Raymond’s sister Colleen had the following to share about her brother:
I remember when my big brother Gord, who eventually preferred to go by Dale, surprised me by showing up at my school choir’s performance in a distant city, where he lived at the time. He walked up to the stage and waved, before we started singing, so I knew he was there for me when our parents couldn’t be. He hasn’t shown up for the past 40 years, but our family has never stopped hoping he will. If anyone has any information about Dale, no matter how small, please call the detectives. It could make all the difference.
This is the performance Colleen remembers when Dale surprised her.
https://www.nwpolice.org/media/School-choir-performance-1969-1970.m4a
The Specialized Investigations Unit works to progress historical missing persons investigations. Investigators have recently been able to dedicate focused time to advancing this file. If you have any information about Mr. Raymond, please call the New Westminster Police Department at 604-525-5411.

title: Criminal Charges approved against New Westminster Police Officer
content:
New Westminster –
Earlier today, the BC Prosecution Service announced the laying of criminal charges against a sworn member of the New Westminster Police Department. This release is intended to provide some additional context.
In May of 2025, the New Westminster Police Department became aware of allegations of misconduct committed by one of its officers. This information was immediately reported to the Office of the Police Complaint Commissioner (OPCC) and the officer was suspended from duty. The New Westminster Police Department also requested that the Abbotsford Police Department conduct an external criminal investigation. In August of 2025, the New Westminster Police Board amended the officer’s suspension to being without pay.
On June 25, 2026 the BC Prosecution Service announced that Constable Hardeep Purba, hired by the NWPD in April of 2024, has been now charged with the following offences:
Two counts of Breach of Trust, contrary to Section 122 of the Criminal Code.
“Upon becoming aware of the allegations, we took immediate steps to ensure this officer was suspended from duty so he did not have further contact with the public,” stated Chief Constable Paul Hyland, “These allegations absolutely do not represent the values, professionalism, or standards I expect of my staff, and I hope that this doesn’t overshadow the important work they do every day.”
As this matter is now before the courts, the NWPD will not be in a position to provide further comment.

title: NWPD respond to weapons call near 14th Street and 8th Avenue
content:
New Westminster
– At approximately 8:15 am on June 24th, the New Westminster Police Department received a 9-1-1 call from someone who shared that as they were driving in the area of 14th Street and 8th Avenue, they saw a man with what they believed to be a firearm.
New Westminster Police Department officers flooded the area to search for anyone matching the suspect description. Officers notified the nearby school, and for the next hour there was a significant police presence in the area. NWPD drones searched for the suspect from above and officers canvassed the area for CCTV footage.
“After thoroughly searching the area, no one matching the suspect description was found,” stated Sergeant Andrew Leaver. “This caller did the right thing, and our response demonstrates how seriously we take these kinds of calls.”
The New Westminster Police Department would like to remind the public that if they see anything that causes them immediate concern for their safety or the safety of others to call 9-1-1.

title: Police respond to call about suspected grenade at Queensborough dog park
content:
New Westminster –
On July 1 at approximately 10:00am the New Westminster Police Department received a 9-1-1 call from someone who described seeing what appeared to be a grenade at Ryall Park inside the dog park area. Officers rushed to the location and secured the scene.
Officers utilized an NWPD drone and conducted a search of the area. After a thorough search, the suspicious object was located and it was determined to be a butane lighter in the shape of a grenade. The park reopened shortly after officers determined there was no threat.
“These lighters are as foolish as they are dangerous,” stated Sergeant Andrew Leaver. “These create unnecessary fear. Nothing about them is clever or funny.”
Officers would like to thank park users for their patience while officers worked in the area. The New Westminster Police Department has issued numerous warnings about novelty lighters shaped as weapons. These lighters pose a risk to the person using them and everyone around them as they are routinely mistaken for real weapons. These lighters result in public distress, calls to 9-1-1, and significant police response.

title: Police respond to potentially explosive device on Ash Street
content:
New Westminster –
On July 9 at approximately 4:00pm the New Westminster Police Department received a 9-1-1 call from someone who described finding what they believed could be an explosive device in the 300 block of Ash Street. Officers rushed to the location, secured the scene, and closed the 300 block of Ash Street to all traffic. Out of an abundance of caution, some residents were asked to leave their suites from a nearby multi-family building.
Officers worked in partnership with the BC RCMP Explosives Disposal Unit to safely remove the object to a secure location. Police worked in the area for approximately three hours, which included utilizing a police drone.
“We’d like to thank residents for their cooperation as we worked to ensure their safety,” stated Sergeant Andrew Leaver. “We treat every threat as real until we can determine otherwise. While this does cause a disruption, it’s paramount that we take steps to keep people safe.”
The investigation is in the early stages and explosives experts are examining the device recovered from Ash Street. The New Westminster Police Department would like to thank residents and drivers for their patience. Additionally, officers thank our partners at the RCMP Explosives Disposal Unit for their assistance and expertise. If you know anything about the suspected explosive device and have not spoken to police you are asked to call 604-525-5411.

title: East Columbia Street closed for several hours after truck drives off road
content:
New Westminster
– On July 20 at approximately 2:00pm, the New Westminster Police Department received reports of a single vehicle collision at the intersection of Holmes Street and East Columbia Street. A mid-sized roll-off bin truck was travelling down Holmes Street, but did not stop at the intersection of East Columbia Street, travelled through the intersection and over the embankment.
“Thankfully, no one was seriously injured from this collision,” stated Media Relations Officer Sergeant Andrew Leaver. “The New Westminster Police Department Commercial Vehicle Enforcement Unit is currently investigating to determine if there was a mechanical problem with the truck or if it was driver error.”
BC Emergency Health Services Paramedics transported the driver to hospital with minor injuries. Crews spent several hours removing the vehicle from the embankment. While Holmes Street is not a truck route, trucks are permitted to make deliveries on that street. Officers thank the public for their patience.
The New Westminster Police Department created the Commercial Vehicle Enforcement Unit in 2014. The unit employs two experienced commercial vehicle enforcement officers who work in partnership with other commercial vehicle enforcement teams across the region. In addition to inspecting commercial vehicles to ensure they comply with the Commercial Transport Act and the Motor Vehicle Act, the team enforces truck routes throughout the city.

title: Collision investigation leads to arrest, recovery of stolen vehicle, and seizure of firearm
content:
New Westminster –
At approximately 2:00am on July 25, the New Westminster Police Department responded to a 9-1-1 call from someone sharing he saw a truck hit a barrier on the Queensbrough Bridge at a high rate of speed. An officer located the driver, passenger, and damaged vehicle in a nearby parking lot. The officer determined the vehicle had been reported stolen and the two men were arrested. When searched by police, one suspect was in possession of a loaded firearm.
“This underscores how the public serves as our eyes and ears,” stated Sergeant Andrew Leaver. “They have trust that the New Westminster Police Department will attend and investigate. In this case, it resulted in a dangerous weapon being taken off our streets.”
One man was released at the scene and the second suspect was transported to cells. He was released with numerous conditions. It is anticipated that charges related to stolen property and firearms will be forwarded to Crown counsel.
The New Westminster Police Department would like to than the witnesses who called police after observing the collision. If you are witnessing a crime in progress, fear for your safety, or the safety of others, please call 9-1-1.

title: New Westminster Police Department officers rescue residents from apartment fire
content:
New Westminster
– On July 30 at approximately 6:00pm, New Westminster Police Department officers were working in the 800 block of 5th Avenue when they became aware of a nearby apartment fire. As officers approached the building, they could see numerous older adults leaning outside of their windows in an effort to avoid the smoke.
Officers entered the burning building alongside their colleagues from the New Westminster Fire and Rescue Service and assisted 15 residents make their way to safety. Several residents were unable to move and required multiple first responders to carry them to safety. Two officers went to hospital for smoke inhalation but have since been released.
“The actions of our officers reflect the very best of policing,” stated Media Relations Officer Sergeant Andrew Leaver. “Their quick response and selfless efforts helped these residents escape an incredibly dangerous situation.”
The role of first responders includes taking whatever actions are necessary in the moment to ensure public safety. The New Westminster Police Department are supporting the New Westminster Fire and Rescue Service with securing the scene until they complete their work.

title: Man arrested after allegedly brandishing firearm at coffee shop patron
content:
New Westminster
– At approximately 6:00am on July 30, the New Westminster Police Department responded to a 9-1-1 call after someone brandished a firearm at a coffee shop patron on the patio of a business in the Columbia Square shopping centre. Police determined the suspect fled across Columbia Street, through a hole in the fence, and across the railway tracks.
Officers rushed to the area to locate the suspect. An NWPD drone was deployed to aid in the search. The suspect was located alongside the train tracks in the bushes and arrested thanks to the help of the Lower Mainland District Integrated Police Dog Service. At the time of his arrest the suspect was found to be in possession of prohibited weapons, knives, and cans of bear spray. An area search later located the firearm.
“This is the second time within a week our officers have seized a firearm,” stated Sergeant Andrew Leaver. “This was a quick and coordinated response by New Westminster Police Department officers.”
The New Westminster Police Department would like to thank the Lower Mainland District Integrated Police Dog Service. The handler and the K9 were instrumental in the arrest and recovery of the firearm. Additionally, the New Westminster Police Department would like to thank the witness who called 9-1-1 quickly as it allowed officers to arrive on scene while the suspect was still in the nearby area.

title: Police warn of fraudulent QR codes on parking meters
content:
New Westminster –
The New Westminster Police Department is warning the public about fraudulent QR codes attached to parking meters throughout the city.
Police have received numerous calls from victims who have scanned the QR codes labelled “scan to pay” on the front of the meters, and were directed to a seemingly legitimate site to enter their credit card information to complete the parking transaction. The victims later noticed that they had large amounts of money withdrawn from their personal bank accounts. One victim had $2,000 withdrawn from their account.
New Westminster Police Department officers are investigating the source of these stickers and encouraging anyone who has used them to pay for parking in the last five days to check their bank accounts and report any suspicious activity to police and their banks.
“Our officers have already removed numerous stickers on meters throughout the city” stated Media Relations Officer Sergeant Andrew Leaver. “We would like to remind the public to be vigilant. While the stickers may appear legitimate, acceptable forms of payment are printed on signs above or on the meter.”
The City of New Westminster does not use QR codes as a payment method for parking. The New Westminster Police Department asks community members to share news of this scam with friends and loved ones.
